coach_verdict: Your TSB is in the positive zone (+3.4), meaning you are fully adapted to recent training and primed for high-quality load. I am prescribing Option 1: 5km Specific VO2max Running Intervals. This directly targets your key performance milestone, leveraging your fresh physiological state to hit high-intensity paces before fatigue sets in. Keep the execution sharp and strict.

priority_1.workout_details: Warm-up: 15 minutes of Zone 2 running, followed by 3x 50m strides. Main Set: 5x 1000m running at target 5km race pace (RPE 9/10). Recovery: 3 minutes of active recovery jog (Zone 1) between each repetition. Cool-down: 10 minutes of light jogging and dynamic stretching.
priority_1.reason: Highest priority today because the positive TSB and recovered state allow you to execute high-intensity running quality without risking injury. Directly targets your 5km speed and VO2max pace.

priority_2.workout_details: Warm-up: 15 minutes progressive spin to Zone 2 with 3x 30-sec high-cadence spin-ups. Main Set: 3x 12 minutes at 232W (90% of FTP). Recovery: 4 minutes of light spinning (<130W) between sets. Cool-down: 10 minutes of easy spinning.
priority_2.reason: Focuses on your 20-minute power and FTP development. Sweet spot training builds CTL efficiently with lower neuromuscular fatigue than Zone 5, making it an excellent aerobic threshold builder.

priority_3.workout_details: Warm-up: 10 minutes of dynamic mobility (90/90 hips, active planks). Main Set: 1. Barbell Back Squats: 3 sets of 5 reps at 80% 1RM. 2. Romanian Deadlifts: 3 sets of 8 reps. 3. Dumbbell Overhead Press: 3 sets of 6 reps. 4. Heavy Sandbag Carries (70kg): 3 runs of 50 meters. Core: 3 rounds of 60-second Plank variations.
priority_3.reason: Provides the essential muscular torque needed for cycling power transfer and structural resilience for high-impact running. Ideal if you feel any minor lower-limb joint tightness that makes running intervals inadvisable today.
